section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Average Rate of Change
section_1.content: Recall the slope formula. Introduce a cheetah sprinting: the average speed is (Total Distance) / (Total Time) between two points. Visually, this is the slope of the secant line connecting two points on a distance-time curve.
section_1.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed = 20 m/s. Show a line segment connecting (0,0) and (5,100) on a graph.

section_2.title: The Problem of 'Instantaneous'
section_2.content: Challenge the student: If the cheetah isn't running at a constant speed, how fast is it going at exactly 2 seconds? Introduce the 'zoom-in' concept. As the two points on the graph get closer, the secant line approaches the tangent line.
section_2.example: Visual animation: A secant line segment shrinks as the second point slides toward the first point until the interval becomes near-zero.

section_3.title: Defining the Derivative via Limits
section_3.content: Define the derivative as the limit of the average rate of change as the interval approaches zero. Formally introduce the notation f'(x) = lim (h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Emphasize that this is the slope of the tangent line.
section_3.example: Use a ball thrown into the air. Show how the slope of the position curve changes from positive (rising) to zero (peak) to negative (falling).

section_4.title: Graphical Interpretation and Application
section_4.content: Summarize the bridge between algebra and geometry: The derivative at a point = Slope of the Tangent Line = Instantaneous Rate of Change. Use a car's speedometer to illustrate this real-world application.
section_4.example: A car speedometer displays the instantaneous rate of change of position; it doesn't wait for a distance interval to pass, it measures the 'now'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map to right side of screen: x > 0
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 1.8 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Average Rate of Change", [
            "Average speed is distance divided by time.", 
            "Visualize the slope of a secant line.", 
            "Cheetah sprints 100 meters in 5 seconds."
        ])
        
        # Create Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 5, 1], axis_config={"color": "#FFFFFF"}).scale(0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color the first line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color the second line
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2.5], color="#FFFF00")
        p = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 1), color="#00FFFF")
        q = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 4), color="#00FFFF")
        secant = Line(axes.c2p(1, 1), axes.c2p(2, 4), color="#FF00FF")
        
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(p), FadeIn(q))
        self.play(Create(secant))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color the third line
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        slope_label = MathTex(r"m = \frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}", color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, 'A4')
        self.play(Write(slope_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
